question: Can black holes move through space?
short_answer: Yes, black holes move through space following galactic gravitational orbits and can be ejected at high speeds during asymmetric supernova explosions or galaxy mergers.
full_explanation: Rogue black holes travel through the Milky Way at speeds exceeding 100 km/s, orbiting the galactic center just like ordinary stars.
